newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crude flat with NYMEX amid thin talk.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crude flat with NYMEX amid thin talk.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude oil prices were flat Tuesday, as local traders awaited inventory reports or attended an industry function, dealers said.
The American Petroleum Institute (API) reported crude oil inventories in the West Coast region rose 311,000 barrels last week, a negligible number, according to local traders.
The largest producer of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude, the regional benchmark, offered the grade at $1.60 off July West Texas Intermediate (WTI) but saw no takers in a thin market.
No trades have transpired this week with many refiners at a rafting trip sponsored by Tosco Corp Monday and Tuesday.
Pressure has mounted to sell ANS below the market's current $1.75 diffential. Traders heard rumors that ANS' largest seller has diverted supplies west in an attempt to clear out inventories.
The producer allegedly sold a pipeline cargo of ANS to a Midwest refinery at $2.00 under July WTI, the equivalent of $4.00 under into the West Coast, traders said.
Buyers expect the next ANS cargo to sell wider than $2.50 barrel off July WTI.
Crude oil futures lent little support to the prompt market, with the July delivery eased one cent a barrel Tuesday.
